brownian.banner:
USAGE:
brownian motion 1 fi fo chans dur att dec plo phi pstart sstart step sstep tick seed
[-aarange] [-mminamp] [-saslope] [-ddslope] [-l]
OR
brownian motion 2 fi fo chans dur plo phi pstart sstart step sstep tick seed
[-aarange] [-mminamp] [-l]

Generate texture of sampled elements following brownian motion in pitch and space.

FI      (Mono) Source to be read at different speeds to generate output events.
        MODE 1: src must start & end at sampval 0.0 : sampled as a waveform.
        MODE 2: src can be anything, whole src is transposed for output events..
                (In mode 2, very int source may take very long time to finish).
FO      Output file.
CHANS   Number of channels in output file.
DUR     (Max) duration of output file.
ATT*    Rise time of events (Mode 1 only).
DEC*    Decay time of events (Mode 1 only).
PLO*    Bottom of pitch range (MIDI).
PHI*    Top of pitch range (MIDI).
PSTART  Initial pitch (MIDI).
SSTART  Initial spatial position (numbering chans 1 - N) (ignored if mono output).
STEP*   Maximum pitch step between events.
SSTEP*  Max spatial step between events (fraction of distance between channels).
TICK*   (Average) Time between events.
SEED    Seed (initialises random vals. Gives reproducible random sequence).
ARANGE* Max loudness step between events, in dB (default = min = 0: max = 96dB).
MINAMP* Min loudness (Range  >0 to 96dB). default = 0 = NO minimum.
        (Only comes into play if "ARANGE" is > 0).
        (If min > 0: if amp falls to -min dB, levels 'bounce' off the min value).
        (If min = 0: no min set, & if level falls to -96dB, sounds stream halts).
(Mode 1 only)
ASLOPE* attack slope: < 1 rise fast then slows  : > 1 rise slow then faster.
DSLOPE* decay slope:  < 1 fall slow then faster : > 1 fall fast then slows.
        Slope ranges are 0.1 to 10.

-l      loudspeakers arrayed in a line. (Default: arrayed in a "circle").

All items marked with "*" can vary though time.

cascade.banner:
USAGE: cascade cascade 1-5  inf outf clipsize  echos clipmax [-eechosmax] 
OR:    cascade cascade 6-10 inf outf cuts echos [-eechosmax]

AND:   [-rrand] [-sseed] [-Nshredno -Cshredcnt -a] [-l] [-n]

Successive segments of src are repeat-echoed, and echosets superimposed on src.

Modes
1,6:  N-channels in -> N channels out: Every echo in same N-channels.
2,7:  Mono (left in output)  ->stereo: Echosets pan to right.
3,8:  Mono (centre in output)->stereo: Echosets pan alternately to L and R.
4,9:  Mono (ch1 in output) -> 8chan: Every echo steps R, to next channel.
5,10: Mono (ch1 in outout) -> 8chan: Echos of 1st echoset step R,next set step L,etc.

CLIPSIZE (Modes 1-5)  Duration of segments to echo. Time-variable.
or       (Range .005 to 60 secs)
CUTS     (Modes 6-10) Textfile of (successive) src cut-times, creating segs to echo.

ECHOS    Number of echos. Time-variable. (Range 1 to 64)

CLIPMAX  Max duration of clips (time-variable). "CLIPSIZE" now read as minimum.
         Actual clipsize is a random val between "clipsize" and "clipmax".
         If "clipmax" is set to zero, it is ignored.

ECHOSMAX Max number of echos (time-variable). "ECHOS" now read as minimum.
         Actual number of echos is a random val between "echos" and "echosmax".
         If "echosmax" is set to zero, it is ignored.

RAND     Randomise timesteps between echos in echo-set: Range 0-1, time-variable.
SEED     With same non-zero value, randomised vals are exactly same on new pass.

SHREDNO  In each echo-stream, cut previous echo into "shredno" parts,
         and random-shuffle parts to make next echo. Range 2-16,time-variable.
SHREDCNT No of shreds to do, to create next echo element. Range 1-16,time-variable.
         BOTH "shredno" and "shredcnt" must be set for shredding to take place.
-a   Also shred original clip. Only valid if "shredno" & "shredcnt" set.

-l   Echos decay linearly in level (default, log decay - initial decays faster).
-n   If output low, normalise it. (high output is normalised by default).

ceracu.banner:
USAGE:
ceracu ceracu inf outf cyclcnts mincycdur chans outdur echo echshift [-o] [-l]

Repeat src in several cyclestreams that resynchronise after specified counts.
One complete pass is a "resync-cycle". e.g. for 10 12 15
Source repeat 10,12 and 15 times before cyclestreams resynchronise ....
IF source sound is "A", cyclestreams would be ....
A     A     A     A     A     A     A     A     A     A     A (10 times)
A    A    A    A    A    A    A    A    A    A    A    A    A (12 times)
A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A   A (15 times)
|--------------------------Resync cycle --------------------|
|---| = Mincycdur (see below)

CYCLECNTS A list of integers, being
          the number of repeats in each cyclestream before the streams resync.
MINCYCDUR Time before the first repeat in the fastest cyclestream.
          If set to ZERO, assumed to be the duration of the input sound.
CHANS:    Number of channels in output. (Not ness same as number of cyclestreams)
OUTDUR    Duration of output. (If set to ZERO, outputs a single resync-cycle).
          Process always outputs a WHOLE NUMBER of complete resync-cycles,
          equal to or greater than the specified output duration.
          If true duration > 1 hour, sound curtailed, unless "-o" flag set.
ECHO      Single-echo-delay of entire output, in secs (Set to zero for no echo).
ECHSHIFT  Spatial offset of echo-delay (an integer value). (Ignored if no echo)
          1 = 1 chan to right; 2 = 2 chans to right; -1 = 1 channel to left; etc
-o        Override duration restriction, to produce all resync-cycles (CARE!).
-l        Output channels arranged linearly (default: arranged in a circle).

crumble.banner:
USAGE: crumble sound 1 inf outf stt dur1 dur2      params
OR:    crumble sound 2 inf outf stt dur1 dur2 dur3 params

where PARAMS are
orient size rand iscat oscat ostrch pscat seed [-ssplice] [-ttail]

Project a MONO source on all channels of multichan output, then segment it,
and distribute the segments over smaller and smaller groups of channels.

Mode 1 gives 8-channel output  (ochans = 8)
Mode 2 gives 16-channel output (ochans = 16)

STT     Start time of crumbling.
DUR1    Duration of section where signal split into 2 images.
DUR2    Duration of section where signal split into 4 images.
DUR3    (Mode 2) Duration of section where signal split into 8 images.
ORIENT  Input image first splits onto 2 blocks each of ochans/2 adjacent chans.
        (1) chan "ori" with adjacent clockwise channels,
        (2) remaining channels.
SIZE*   (Average) duration of cut segments.
RAND*   Randomisation of segment size. (Range 0 - 1)
        Max(1) modifies "siz" randomly between siz/2 and (3*siz)/2
ISCAT*  Scattering (in source) of start-time of next segment cut. (Range 0 - 1)
        Cut-time in source always advances.
        With no scatter, step to next cut-time = length of previous segment cut.
        With max "isct"(1) step  by random time between 0 and previous-seglen.
OSCAT*  Scattering (in output) of time-placement of segment used.(Range 0 - 1)
        Time in output always advances.
        With no scatter, step to next output-time = length of last segment cut.
        With max "osct"(1) step by random time between >0 and previous-seglen.
OSTRCH* Stretching of time-placement in output. (Range 1 - 64)
        Step to next sgement-placement in output, is multiplied by ostr.
        ostr > 1 should generate silent gaps in the output.
PSCAT*  Pitch variation of output segments (Semitones).
        for e.g. psct=3, pitch varies at random between +3 and -3 semitones.
SEED    Same seed value gives identical output on successive process runs.
SPLICE  Length of splices which cut the segments (in millseconds).
TAIL*   Length of any exponential tail on segments (in millseconds).

Parameters marked with "*" can vary over time (i.e. time in the outfile).

crystal.banner:
crystal rotate 1-10 fi [fi2 fi3..] fo vdat rota rotb twidth tstep dur plo phi
        [-ppass -sstop] [-afatt] [-Pfpresc] [-Ffslope] [-Ssslope]

Generate N snd-events based on position of N vertices of a crystal,
Then rotate crystal in 3-d space, and generate another group of N events, etc.
X coord -> time &, if stereo, space-position; Y -> pitch; Z -> brightness..i.e.
Z-far snds lopass-filtrd mixed to orig; Z-close snds, 8va up, stacked on orig.

FI        One Mono infile, multiply-read (with delay), generating out-events.
          OR N mono infiles, generating different events for N vertices.
FO        Output file.
VDAT      Data file contains
          (1) Triples, being (initial) X,Y,Z, coords of CRYSTAL VERTICES.
                 Range > -1 to <1. Xsquared + Ysqrd + Zsqrd < 1 for all vertices.
          (2) Time-val pairs defining envelope imposed on sound events.
                 Times start at 0 & increase. Final time = duration of events.
                 Value range 0 to 1. First and last values must be zero.
ROTA,ROTB Rotate speed in xy_plane, & xz_plane, revs per sec (Range -10.00 to 10.00)
TWIDTH    Max time between onsets of 1st and last event in any N-events group.
TSTEP     Time-step between each sampling of all N vertices of rotating-crystal.
DUR       Total duration of output (must be greater than TSTEP and TWIDTH).
PLO,PHI   Minimum and Maximum (MIDI) pitch of any event.
PASS,STOP Pass+stop bands (Hz) for lopass filter.(stopfrq - passfrq >= 50 Hz).
FATT      Max attenuation produced by filter-stop (dB) Range 0 to -96.
FPRESC    Gain applied to attenuate source before applying filter (0-1).
FSLOPE    Slope curve mixing filtered to unfilt snd (depth). (Range 0.10 to 10.00).
SSLOPE    Slope curve mixing transposed snd to orig (close). (Range 0.10 to 10.00).
          In both cases Linear slope = 1.0
FOG       Generic name for output files.
OUTCNT    Number of rotated-sets to output.
MODES
1  Mono output
2  Stereo output
3  Two chans of 8-chan output, spaced by single channel (here, chans 1 & 3).
4,5,6  Ditto, chan-pair steps clockwise,anticlock or randomly btwn groups-of-events.
7,8,9  Ditto, but pair of chans adjacent (e.g. 1,2 or 5,6).
10     Stereo output: each set-of-vertices output as a separate soundfile.

DISPERSE MONO SIGNAL INTO FRAGMENTS SPREAD OVER N-CHANNEL SPACE.

Mode 2: Output is stereo dispersal (posibly moving) in surround space.

PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE
ETAB     Textfile: Each line is a TIME followed by 7 PAIRS of envelope-data.
         envelope-data represented in form "etime lev"
         where "etime" is relative time WITHIN envelope (values between 0 & 1)
         and "lev" is level at etime (values 0-1). In each envelope-data set
         "lev" must start and end at zero and rise to a max value of 1.0
CHNS     Number of channels in output file (2-16). (Mode 2, multiples of 4 only).
STRMS    No. of spatial positions (streams) for resulting fragments ( >=4 ).
PULSE    Average gap btwn 1 set-of-frags (each in different strm) & next set.
         Disp = 0: all frags in sync at each (possibly randomised) pulse.
         Disp > 0: frags time-scattered around pulse centre. (see below).
EDPTH    Envelope depth. 1: env cuts down to zero, 0.75: cuts 3/4 way to zero,
(+STACK) 0.1: cuts only 1/10 way to zero,   0: env has no effect on source.
         Once depth exceeds 1, fragments begin to stack (but NOT before)
         (i.e. transposed copies added to fragment, synced at envelope peak).
         Depth 2 -> Stack 1: 1st transposed element added at full level.
         Depth 1.5 -> Stack 06.5: 1st transpd element added at 1/2 (0.5) level.
         Depth 2.5 -> Stack 1.5: 1st added at full level, 2nd at 1/2 level etc
STKINT   Interval of (upward) transposition in stack, in semitones (0-12).
         Default(0) is read as octave(12). NO ZEROS in stack brkpoint files.
SEED     If NOT zero, repeating process with same seed gives identical output.
MIN/MAX  Minimum/maximum duration of fragments. If zero, no minimum/maximum.
RRND     Randomisation of read-time in src. Range 0-1.
PRND     Randomisation of pulse-time in output. Range 0-1.
         In both cases, Max(1) scatters in range +- half-duration of pulse.
DISP     Dispersal (scatter) of output timings between different streams.
         If pulse(+prnd) gives time "P", then for disp 0: all frags are at "P"
         for disp 1: frags scattered within max range (+- half-dur of pulse).
LRND     Randomisation of levels (volume) of fragments. Range  0 - 1.
         0: All frags full level.  1: Frags at random levels between 0 & full.
ERND     Randomisation of envelope used. A time range (trange).
         Event at "now" reads etable at randtime btwn "now" & now-minus-trange.
SRND     Randomisation of stack. Range 0 - 1 (NB stack value (S) = DEPTH-1)
         0: Stack value is S.   1: Stack val selected at random between 0 & S.
TRND     Random tranpose of fragments. Range 0-1200 cents (1 octave upwards).
         Event pitch randomised between pitch+trnd and pitch-trnd.
-z       Permit stacking of very short events. Default = forbid, prevent clipping.
-l       For more than 2 output chans, lspkrs assumed to encircle listeners,
         with a single lspkr at centre front.
         Setting -l flag assumes linear array, with leftmost+rightmost lspkrs.

NB: STKINT, MAX, RRND, LRND, SRND and TRND are INACTIVE if depth < 1.
All these params can timevary EXCEPT "chns", "strms" & "seed".

PRESS KEY "2" TO SEE EXTRA OPTIONS AVAILABLE IN MODE 2
OR ANY OTHER KEY TO FINISH.

inf and outf are input and output analysis files.

All the channels of the analysis are partitioned into N mutually exclusive sets
with channels assigned at random to each set. These sets form a complete group.
Then channels in the first set are played, for "setdur" windows,
at which point channels in the 2nd set are played for "setdur" windows and so on.
(As this happens, we are progressing through the original files at its original rate
the process determining merely which channels are used - the others being zeroed).
Once all N sets are exhausted, a new group is made by random partition, and so on.

           (e.g. for grpdiv = 4, process partitions chans randomly
           among 4 sets with [totalchans/4] channels per set).
           Must be an exact divisior of the channelcnt.
SETDUR     Number of windows for which a set-of-channels persists
           before we switch to next set-of-chans (Range 1-1024)
PITCHSHIFT Max range of random +- pitch shifting of each chanset (in semitones)
           (Range 0 to 12.0 : Default 0)
DURRAND    Randomisation of setdur between 1 and setdur (Range 0 - 1).
DIVRAND    Randomise number of channels in each set in a group (Range 0 - 1).

For each output event, source played at 1 or more spatial locations, SYNCHRONOUSLY.

          and, if the "-e" flag is set, the proportion of empty events increases.

RAND      Randomisation of step size (0-1).

USAGE: peak extract
1   analfile outf winsiz peak floor lo hi [-htune] [-a] [-m] [-q] [-z]
2-4 analfile outf winsiz peak floor lo hi [-htune] [-a] [-m] [-q] [-z] [-f]

MODE 1 Output time and frq:amp for peaks in each window.
          Number of peaks may vary from window to window.
MODE 2 Assign peaks to max number of pitch-streams.
          Number of streams = max number of peaks found in any of windows.
          Where windows have too few peaks to fit all these streams,
          frq vals (at zero amplitude) at the (current) best-fit frq 
          are set in the stream. All peaks will lie in some stream.
MODE 3 Assign peaks to most prominent pitch-streams.
          This mode assumes spectrum is relatively constant.
          It parses entire file, counting peaks in every semitone interval.
          Then uses most visited semitones as stream centres.
          Time-varying pitch(amp) data then assigned to those streams.
          Peaks may be discarded where insufficient streams available.
MODE 4 Find streams as mode 3, then get average pitch + relative amp
          of each stream. Output does not vary through time.

winsiz semitone width of window used to search for peaks in spectrum.
       (Range 1 - 96)
peak   To retain as peak, channel amp must be 'peak' times louder than
       median amp of all channels in window (Range 1 - 1000)
floor  Peaks must exceed a floor amplitude to be retained (Range 0.0001 - 1).
       Entered val is multiplied by max channel amp found anywhere in file.
lo     Minimum frq to accept as a peak (Range analchanwidth - nyquist)
hi     Maximum frq to accept as a peak (Range analchanwidth - nyquist)
tune   If non-zero, any peak which is a harmonic of another peak
       (to within 'tune' semitones accuracy) is discarded (Range 0 - 6).
       If set to zero, all peaks are retained.
-a  Lose the amplitude information:
       If set, amps information discarded.
-m  Output frq information as midi:
-q  Output frq quantised to tempered scale (in quarter-tones):
-z  Mark peak-free segments:
       start/end of peak-free areas marked by (timed) zeros in output.
-f  Output in filter varibank format: This flag cancels the -z flag.
       If -a flag also set, all outputs amps are set to 1.0.

          Events can't overlap, so minimum "contraction" = "shrinkage".

RND       Randomisation of timings AFTER min event separation reached.

1) Unknots (Events gradually moved, in turn, to be time & space equidistant).
2) Knots   (Runs process in reverse).
3) Counts unknotting steps (No output).
There are 5 (possible) stages to the unknotting process....
(1)  Repeat (each) original pattern (optional).
(2)  Repeat (each) specified combination of patterns (optional).
(3)  Repeat the combination of all patterns (optional).
(4)  Unknot the combined pattern.
(5)  Repeat the unknotted pattern (optional).
Input patterns have lines each with 4 entries "time  MIDI  level  pos"
time :     must start at zero and not decrease.
MIDI :     vals between 0 & 127, where convention is 0 indicates a silent file.
level:     lies between >0 and 1.
pos  :     position in an 8-channel space, range 0 to 8 (fractional values OK).
PARAMETERS:
COMBOS    Textfile List of pattern combos to use. (or zero, if no combos used)
          Each line lists 2 or more patterns to combine.
Number of repetitions of......
R_PATS    each original pattern    (Unknot, placed at start : Knot, placed at end).
R_COMBOS  each pattern combination.(Unknot, placed next : Knot, placed penultimate).
R_ALL     combined initial pattern.
R_UNKNOTS each unknotting/knotting step.
R_GOAL    goal pattern.
SPACETYP  Type of spatial distribution for unknotted pattern.
  0  No spatial redistribution.        3  Rotate anticlock between channels.
  1  Alternating between channels.     4  Rotate clock-anticlock between channels.
  2  Rotate clockwise between chans.   5  Rotate anticlock-clock between channels.
(Redistributions to mono, tutti etc, can be made by a mix to mono, & crossfading).
CHA       First channel for spacetyp redistribution.
CHB       Second channel for spacetyp redistribution.
MIN       Event-Duration-differences read as "zero" (pulse "regular" = unknotted).
CLIP      Number of events to reposition at each (un)knotting step (default 1).
-e        Spatial redistribution starts at (un)knotting end.
          (default: ....starts at (un)knotting start.)
-t        Output data with titles and spacing to identify patterns being output.

USAGE:

Play source, with specified brief moments glissing up or down.

TIMES  Textfile listing times of verge-attacks.

TRANS  Semitone transposition at start of verge. (Defuault 5).
EXP    slope of glissi (1(dflt) to 8) : higher vals gliss faster.
DUR    duration of glissi, in mS. (default 100)

waveform.banner:
USAGE: waveform make 1 infile outfile time cnt.
OR:    waveform make 2 infile outfile time dur.
OR:    waveform make 3 infile outfile time dur balance.

Generate a wavetable from existing sound.

Input file must be MONO.

Mode 1 extracts a group of half-wavesets at specified time in infile.
Mode 2 extracts given duration of source, cutting at zero-crossing.
Mode 3 combines specified duration-segment of infile with a sinusoid.

CNT     Number of half-wavesets to extract.
DUR     Duration, in mS, of sound-clip to extract.
TIME    Time in infile where data is extracted.
BALANCE Level of extracted material relative to imposed sinusoid.

In each case, the cut segment is abutted to its inversion,
making a symmetric wavecycle (and doubling its duration).
In Modes 1 & 2 this forms the output.
In Mode 3 this is superimposed on a sinusoid of wavelength DUR * 2.

wrappage.banner:
GRANULAR RECONSTITUTION OF ONE OR MORE SOUNDFILES OVER MULTICHANNEL SPACE.

USAGE       (name of outfile must NOT end with a '1')
wrappage wrappage infile [infile2 ...] outfile centre outchans spread depth
veloc hveloc dens hdens gsize hgsize pshift hpshift amp hamp bsplice hbsplice
esplice hesplice  range jitter outlength [-bmult] [-e] [-o]

CENTRE:    central position of output image in outputfile. (Range 0-outchans).
           Centre values below 1 are positions between last chan and 1st chan.
           Numeric, or a file of triples "time   centre   direction". Direction 
           (1 clockwise, -1 anticlock) is of centre's move from previous position.
OUTCHANS:  Number of channels in output file.
SPREAD:    Width (from far left to far right) of spatialisation around centre.
DEPTH:     No of channels with sound, behind leading edges of spread.
           (Will always be forced to <= half the spread value).
VELOC:     speed of advance in infiles, relative to outfile. (>=0)
           inverse of timestretch, (permits infinite timestretch).
DENS:      grain overlap (>0 : <1 leaves intergrain silence)
           Extremely small values don't perform predictably.
GSIZE:     grainsize in MS (must be > 2 * splicelen) (Default 50)
PSHIFT:    pitchshift in +|- (fractions of) semitones.
AMP:       gain on grains (range 0-1) (Default 1.0)
           use if amp variation required (over a range &/or in time)
BSPLICE:   grain-startsplice length,in MS (Default 5)
ESPLICE:   grain-endsplice length,in MS (Default 5)
RANGE:     of search for nextgrain (in mS), before infile 'now'  (Default 0).
JITTER:    Randomisation of grain position (Range 0-1) Default (0.50).
OUTLENGTH: max outfile length (if end of data not reached).
           Set to zero (Default) to ignore.
           BUT if VELOCITY is ANYWHERE 0: OUTLENGTH must be given.

HVELOC,HDENS,HGSIZE,HPSHIFT,HAMP,HBSPLICE,HESPLICE
allow a range of values to be specified for any of these params. e.g. With
PSHIFT & HPSHIFT set, random pitchshift chosen between these limits.
AND NB PSHIFT & HPSHIFT can both vary through time.

All params, except OUTLENGTH, OUTCHANS, can vary through time.

MULT      Long silences in output may require larger buffers to be used
          "Mult" enlarges output buffers "mult" times. 
-e        Use exponential splices. Default, linear.
-o        Velocity params ALWAYS read relative to time in INPUT file.
          Other params normally read relative to time in INPUT file.
          Flag forces them to be read relative to time in OUTPUT file.
